visibility: AUTHOR ONLY. Independent reviewer must solve the learner reading before opening this file.
independent_translation: God also said, “Let the waters now bring forth swimming kinds, alive with life, and flying kinds over the earth under the firmament of heaven.” And God then created the great whales, and all living and moving kinds of fish which the waters brought forth according to their forms, and all flying kinds according to their kind; God then saw that it was good. And he blessed them, saying thus, “Increase, and be multiplied, and fill the waters of the sea, and let the birds be multiplied over the earth.” And then evening and morning had come to be, the fifth day.
essential_reading_distinctions: The waters are the subject of Tēon and tugon, not the swimming kinds.
The relative ðe is the object of tugon; original notes12–13 expressly distinguish it from the subject article.
Swimmendu/flēogendu/libbendu are actual neuter accusative plurals; cynn/fisccynn are plural in these phrases despite zero nominal ending.
Blētsode has an understood continuing subject God and object hīe them.
First three commands address a plural you; birds then occur as third-person subject with bēon.
Sǣ is source feminine genitive modifying wæteru; it is not a locative in the sea.
The closing become formula is intransitive/resultative, not a passive of create.
acceptable_translation_limits: Kinds/species of swimmers/flyers can idiomatically render the participial noun phrases.
Cucu on līfe is deliberately redundant in a literal rendering; living or alive is enough in smooth English if the supplied source form is understood.
Forms/kinds are supported readings of hīwum; appearance is possible lexical discussion but should not replace the stated kind classification without explaining the choice.
Let ... be multiplied can be rendered may ... multiply in idiomatic English only if the passive form and its target are separately recognized.
